title: Backend senior scenario build vs buy
topic: Backend senior scenario build vs buy
question: Your team needs full-text search over product data, and the launch deadline is six weeks out. Do you build a custom search index or adopt a managed search service like Elasticsearch/Algolia? How do you actually decide, under time pressure, rather than just picking whichever you're more comfortable with?
idealAnswer:
Frames the decision around the team's actual constraints, not a generic pros/cons list: six weeks strongly favors adopting something proven, since building and hardening a custom index (relevance tuning, scaling, operational maturity) rarely fits that timeline well even for an experienced team

Weighs the real cost of 'buy', not just licensing, but the ongoing operational burden of a new piece of infrastructure the team has never run, and evaluates whether that's a reasonable ask alongside everything else in flight

Considers whether the requirement is actually as core and differentiated as it seems, if search relevance itself isn't a competitive differentiator for this product, that argues further toward not spending scarce engineering time building it from scratch

Identifies what would change the calculus, e.g. if the deadline were 6 months rather than 6 weeks, or if search quality were the core product value proposition, note explicitly that the decision isn't universal, it's conditional on the actual constraints

Talks about avoiding lock-in risk with a buy decision by keeping a clean data-access boundary (so the search backend could be swapped later) rather than treating the choice as permanent and irreversible
